_meta.source: ICAR-IIHR (Indian Institute of Horticultural Research) Tomato Production Guide 2022; ICAR-NCIPM Integrated Pest Management for Vegetables; PlantVillage class names mapped to disease entries.
_meta.scope: All 10 PlantVillage tomato classes. Treatments are standard ICAR-recommended IPM (Integrated Pest Management) practices for Indian field conditions.
_meta.disclaimer: Treatment recommendations are advisory only. Dosages and product availability vary by region. Grower should verify with local agricultural extension officer before application.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.description: Water-soaked lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit. Spreads rapidly in warm, wet conditions.
immediate_actions: Remove and destroy severely infected leaves immediately — do not compost
Avoid overhead irrigation; switch to drip if possible to reduce leaf wetness
Disinfect tools with 1% sodium hypochlorite between plants

chemical_treatments.frequency: Spray every 7-10 days; repeat after rain

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.irrigation_note: Current soil moisture is reported separately by the sensor model and is independent of this disease finding. Reduce overhead watering to limit leaf wetness — this is a canopy humidity recommendation, not a response to soil water deficit.

Tomato_Early_blight.description: Concentric-ring dark lesions (target board pattern) on older leaves first. Reduces photosynthetic area and yield.
immediate_actions: Remove lower infected leaves and destroy
Improve canopy air circulation by staking and pruning
Avoid wetting foliage during evening irrigation

chemical_treatments.frequency: Every 7-10 days starting at first symptom

Tomato_Early_blight.irrigation_note: Susceptibility increases under drought conditions — check current sensor moisture reading independently. If moisture is adequate, no irrigation change is needed for this disease alone.

Tomato_Late_blight.description: Fast-spreading water-soaked lesions on leaves and fruit with white sporulation on undersides. Can destroy entire crop within days under humid conditions.
immediate_actions: URGENT: Begin fungicide application immediately — disease spreads explosively
Remove and bag all visibly infected plant material; do not leave on ground
Stop overhead irrigation immediately; switch to drip
Alert neighbouring growers — airborne spores spread rapidly

chemical_treatments.frequency: Every 5-7 days; alternate with contact fungicide

chemical_treatments.product: Copper oxychloride 50% WP (contact, alternate with above)

biological_treatments.dose: 2 ml/litre as preventive only — NOT effective on active infection
biological_treatments.frequency: Weekly preventive; stop once symptoms appear

Tomato_Late_blight.irrigation_note: Current soil moisture is reported separately by the sensor model and is independent of this disease finding. The irrigation recommendation above is about canopy humidity management (switch to drip), NOT about soil water deficit — do not conflate the two.
Tomato_Late_blight.icar_source: ICAR-IIHR Technical Bulletin No. 49; ICAR-NCIPM Advisory 2021

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.description: Pale green/yellow spots on upper leaf surface with olive-green mold on underside. Common in protected cultivation (polyhouses).
immediate_actions: Improve ventilation in polyhouse/greenhouse — reduce humidity below 85%
Remove heavily infected leaves
Reduce plant density if overcrowded
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.irrigation_note: Avoid wetting leaves. Drip irrigation preferred. Ensure good drainage.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Small, circular spots with dark borders and grey-white centres on lower leaves. Progresses upward. Causes premature defoliation reducing fruit quality.
immediate_actions: Remove all lower infected leaves and destroy
Avoid working in field when plants are wet to prevent mechanical spread
Mulch soil to prevent rain-splash dispersal of spores
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.irrigation_note: Use drip irrigation. Reduce canopy humidity. Avoid evening watering.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.description: Tiny mites cause stippling (fine yellow dots) on leaves, leading to bronzing and webbing under leaves. Thrives in hot, dry conditions.
immediate_actions: Inspect undersides of leaves for mites and webbing
Increase irrigation and humidity — spider mites thrive in dry conditions
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural predators (Phytoseiidae)

chemical_treatments.frequency: 2 sprays at 10-day intervals; rotate acaricide class
Do not use more than 2 sprays per season to avoid resistance
Every 7 days; do not apply above 35 C

biological_treatments.dose: Per label; 5-20 per plant depending on infestation
biological_treatments.frequency: Single release; population self-sustains if pesticide exposure reduced

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.irrigation_note: Check current sensor moisture reading independently — increasing irrigation frequency applies only if sensor-reported moisture is below optimal. If sensor shows adequate moisture, no volume change is needed; focus on switching to drip to raise canopy humidity without adding soil water.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.icar_source: ICAR-NCIPM Vegetable IPM Manual; ICAR-IIHR Technical Bulletin No. 49

Tomato__Target_Spot.description: Circular lesions with concentric rings (target pattern) on leaves and fruit. Often confused with Early Blight and Spider Mites — confirm diagnosis before treatment.
immediate_actions: Confirm identification: Target Spot has lighter brown centres vs. Early Blight's darker concentric rings
Remove infected leaves from lower canopy first
NOTE: If this prediction was made alongside a Spider Mites uncertainty flag, visually inspect for webbing under leaves before applying fungicide
Tomato__Target_Spot.irrigation_note: Check current sensor moisture reading independently — this advice applies only if sensor-reported moisture is below optimal. If sensor shows adequate moisture, no irrigation change is needed for this disease alone; drought-stress susceptibility is a background risk, not an immediate action trigger.
Tomato__Target_Spot.confusable_pair_note: Model may confuse with Spider_mites (documented failure mode, 8% of Target_Spot cases). If fusion layer flagged UNCERTAIN_PAIR, recommend visual inspection before fungicide application.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.pathogen: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (Begomovirus), vector: Bemisia tabaci whitefly
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.description: Severe yellowing and upward curling of leaves. Stunted growth. No cure — management focuses on vector control and removal of infected plants.
immediate_actions: URGENT: Remove and destroy all visibly infected plants immediately to prevent virus spread
Install yellow sticky traps (40/acre) to monitor and reduce whitefly population
Establish reflective silver mulch on soil surface to repel whiteflies
Screen nursery transplants — do not introduce infected transplants

chemical_treatments.frequency: At transplanting and 15 days later; avoid flowering period (bee toxicity)
2 sprays at 10-day intervals to control whitefly

chemical_treatments.product: NOTE: No curative antiviral spray exists — all chemical control targets the whitefly vector

biological_treatments.frequency: Weekly spray on underside of leaves where whiteflies congregate

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.irrigation_note: No direct irrigation modification required. Healthy plants are slightly more tolerant.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.icar_source: ICAR-IIHR Technical Bulletin No. 49; ICAR-NCIPM Advisory on TYLCV 2020

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.pathogen: Tomato Mosaic Virus (Tobamovirus), primarily mechanical/contact transmission
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Mosaic pattern (light and dark green patches) on leaves, leaf distortion, and reduced fruit set. Spreads by contact — NOT insect-vectored.
immediate_actions: Wash hands thoroughly with soap before handling plants — primary transmission route is human hands/tools
Remove and destroy infected plants showing severe symptoms
Disinfect all tools with 10% trisodium phosphate solution (not alcohol — alcohol is ineffective against ToMV)
Do not smoke near plants — tobacco is a ToMV reservoir

chemical_treatments.product: No curative chemical treatment available for ToMV
Preventive: use certified virus-free seed and resistant varieties (TM-2 gene)
chemical_treatments.frequency: Seed treatment: hot water at 70C for 2 min before sowing

biological_treatments.product: No biological control available — focus on sanitation

Tomato_healthy.description: Plant appears healthy. No disease detected.
immediate_actions: Continue current management practices
Maintain regular monitoring schedule
